court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Ad-hoc District Judge 2, Satara, Regular Civil Appeal No.153/2006
case_name: Sou. Meena Suresh Mane vs Suresh Gangaram Mane
facts_of_case: Petitioner's application to amend written statement and add person as necessary party was rejected by trial court. Respondent filed petition for divorce under Section 13(1)(i-a) of Hindu Marriage Act,1955. Petitioner denied case including averments about adultery.

legal_principles.principle: In a petition for dissolution of marriage on the ground of adultery, the concerned person should be made party/co-respondent unless there is a valid application to dispense with their joinder.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, prima facie, in the petition for dissolution of marriage on the ground of adultery the concerned person should be made party/co-respondent except the ground mentioned above.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Marriage and Divorce Act — Rule 5
cited_cases: Sou. Meena Suresh Mane vs Suresh Gangaram Mane, (2008)

legal_principles.principle: A court can dispense with the joinder of a person as co-respondent if there is a valid application and sufficient grounds.
legal_principles.held: If application is moved, the court can dispense with the joinder of such person also on the ground reflected above.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Marriage and Divorce Act — Rule 5
cited_cases: Sou. Meena Suresh Mane vs Suresh Gangaram Mane, (2008)

outcome.final_order: Petitioner's application to amend written statement and add person as necessary party was allowed.
